author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  as a follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows, each with the veterinarians holding it, on one page reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: opening the specialty directory at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name
all specialties appear on a single page; the page offers no paging
each specialty names the veterinarians holding it by first name followed by last name, for example Helen Leary
a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by none
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
specialties, and the veterinarians within each, appear in a stable order across repeated requests
no page of the system carries a navigation entry or a link leading to the specialty directory
the specialty directory carries the navigation every page carries, as REQ-SYS-001 requires
every new user-facing wording on the page is present in every supported language, as REQ-LANG-002 requires
non_goals: managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application; NG-2 is unchanged
a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory
searching or filtering the specialty directory
notes: Scope grounded in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1; both owner decisions quoted there are honored. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than blocked on: the visible entry point (deferred by the owner to a follow-up request) and which stable order the page uses. Narrowest readings taken where the request was silent: a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, because the request says every specialty the clinic knows; and the page carries the standard navigation because REQ-SYS-001 binds every page, while gaining no entry of its own.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lives entirely in the existing vet feature package and needs no new module. Two decisions are new ground and are now recorded. First, the Vet-to-Specialty association stays unidirectional: the directory is assembled per request from a new SpecialtyRepository read and the cached VetRepository.findAll() read, rather than from an inverse JPA mapping. Second, the assembly lives in a SpecialtyDirectory value object, not in the controller, because the pattern catalog's Web controller row admits no new business rule and this project has no service layer. Both are recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-specialty-directory-read-model.md, with the resulting contracts in docs/system-design.md#contracts. A specialty no veterinarian holds is unreachable from the veterinarian side today, which is what forces the new repository.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html served by a package-private SpecialtyController returning view name vets/specialtyList; no request parameters, no paging
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data repository over the existing specialties table; it mirrors PetTypeRepository, which returns its lookup rows in name order
VetRepository.findAll() is reused unchanged and stays on the existing vets cache; no new cache is declared in CacheConfiguration
the template renders through fragments/layout, so REQ-SYS-001 navigation is inherited; pass a menu argument matching no nav item so no entry is added or highlighted
Vet.getSpecialties() is EAGER and open-in-view is disabled, so the specialties on a cached Vet are already initialized outside a transaction

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository returning rows in name order; SpecialtyRepository follows this shape
package-private @Controller with a @GetMapping returning a feature-scoped view name; SpecialtyController follows this shape without the pagination helper
Thymeleaf page delegating to fragments/layout with a menu key; the specialty page reuses it with a key matching no nav item
Value object row: SpecialtyDirectory is immutable, equal by value, framework-instantiated by nothing, so the persistence-entity exception does not apply and every closed property binds it in full

risks.risk: BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so joining the specialty read against the Specialty instances hanging off cached Vet objects by object equality silently yields empty groups
risks.mitigation: join on the stored identifier (getId()), never on equals, contains, or set membership

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is a HashSet and VetRepository.findAll() specifies no order, so an unordered assembly renders differently across requests and fails the stable-order criterion
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory imposes a total order from stored values: specialties by name, veterinarians within each by last name then first name

risks.risk: a new message key that does not land in all ten non-English bundles fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest and breaches REQ-LANG-002
risks.mitigation: prefer the existing keys specialties, name, vets, and none, which already cover the heading, both columns, and the held-by-none cell; any genuinely new key lands in messages.properties and all ten locale bundles in the same change

risks.risk: the seed data holds no specialty that zero veterinarians hold, so the edge case cannot be observed through the seeded H2 database
risks.mitigation: cover it in the SpecialtyDirectory unit test with real objects, where the input collections are constructed directly

risks.risk: an inverse mapped-by collection on Specialty would have to be eager under the disabled open-in-view setting, and would then recurse into the serialized veterinarian route
risks.mitigation: rejected in the ADR; Specialty stays a lookup value carrying no collection

notes: No design-doc-autofix records exist in the handoff log, so the autofix audit is skipped. Verdict is new rather than minor: the association direction and the read-model placement are hard-to-reverse choices that durable memory did not answer, and they set the first read-model precedent in this codebase. Not conflicting: NG-2 stays read-only, NG-9 excludes search and this page offers none, and no ADR forbids the capability. The PRD's open question about which stable order the page uses is settled here at design level (specialty by stored name; veterinarian by last name then first name) — no product content is involved. Vocabulary: 'specialty directory' and 'veterinarian' are the PRD's terms; the code short form stays 'vet' for the package and 'Specialty' for the type, per ubiquitous-language.md. Basis for the codebase claims is file reads and greps, not the IntelliJ oracle, which is not connected in this run. Testing note for the implementer: SpecialtyDirectory carries every behavioral criterion and is testable with real objects and no Spring context; MockMvc covers only the route, view name, and model attribute.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests exercises every PRD acceptance criterion with real objects and no framework context: every-specialty-by-name, first+last name display, a specialty held by no veterinarian, a veterinarian holding no specialty omitted, and stable ordering via an equality check across two independently-ordered inputs

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupHoldersWhenTheSpecialtyCameFromASeparateRead directly tests the design's flagged risk (BaseEntity has no equals/hashCode, so the join must be by stored id, not object identity) with a purpose-built aSeparatelyLoadedCopyOf helper

Test data uses the PRD's own example (Helen Leary) and named factory methods (createASpecialty, createAVeterinarian) instead of raw constructors or mystery literals, per the three-tier naming convention

SpecialtyControllerTests follows the existing VetControllerTests precedent for @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean on repositories, consistent with the brief's mocking policy (MockMvc is the sanctioned boundary mock; repository stubs are tolerated existing-pattern, not a new deviation)

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNotBeLinkedFromAnyPage and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryTheNavigationEveryPageCarries give durable, executable coverage of the two PRD decisions (URL-only reachability, but full inherited nav) that are easy to silently regress
No new message keys were introduced (the template reuses specialties/name/vets/none), so REQ-LANG-002 stays covered by the existing I18nPropertiesSyncTest without needing a new test

All method names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school, four-phase structure is clean with blank-line separation and no phase comments, and assertions are fluent AssertJ throughout (extracting, flatExtracting, containsExactly)
./gradlew test passes for both new test classes

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: no dependency was added or changed by this diff, so it widens no supply-chain surface. Recorded for completeness - the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved versions read from ./gradlew dependencies: Spring Boot 4.1.0, spring-webmvc 7.0.8, tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.4, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE, h2 2.4.240. These are not verified against the NVD here - a human or CI should close that check.

Not a finding against the recorded baseline, noted for future load characteristics only: the page reads all specialties uncached and all veterinarians per request with no paging, which the ADR records as deliberate. The specialty and veterinarian tables are clinic-managed rather than caller-grown, and /vets.html's serialized route already performs the same unpaged findAll(), so the change adds no new unbounded-allocation vector.
approved_aspects: Data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static JPQL string with no request-derived value concatenated in; the only other read is the derived VetRepository.findAll(). No injection-into-data-access surface.

XSS: specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (default escaping on). Swept the new template for th:utext and Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) - neither is present, and the only preprocessing in the render path is the pre-existing literal menu link in fragments/layout.html, not a request-derived value.

Exposed surface: /specialties.html is a new GET-only endpoint, documented in prd.md, system-design.md Contracts, and the ADR. It exposes specialty names and veterinarian display names, both already published by /vets.html - no new data class reaches an unauthenticated caller, and management exposure is untouched.
Mass assignment / cross-request trust: the handler takes no request parameter, path variable, or bound command object, so there is no binder to constrain and no identifier carried across requests.

Concurrency: SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton holding only repository references; SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyEntry are records whose compact constructors List.copyOf their collections, so the per-request read model is deeply immutable and safe to share with the view.

Type safety and fail-secure joining: the join keys on the stored identifier via HashMap (null-key tolerant for a transient Specialty) rather than object equality, and Objects.requireNonNull guards the factory boundary with parameter-name-only messages that leak nothing into the exception-rendering error page.
Resource management: the template-walk helper in SpecialtyControllerTests wraps Files.walk in try-with-resources; no production file, stream, or process handling is introduced.

Pattern consistency: specialtyList.html mirrors the existing vetList.html escaping and #{none} fallback structure, and SpecialtyRepository mirrors VetRepository's @Transactional(readOnly = true) read-only shape - the same concern is secured the same way as its neighbour.

author: change-grader
summary: add the specialty directory read model and page

blast_radius.note: Purely additive within the vet package: three new production types, one new template, and doc updates. No existing production file is edited, no route or serialized representation changes, no sensitive path is touched, and the only shared resource reused is the existing vets cache.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: the join keys on Specialty.getId() through a HashMap rather than object equality (correct given BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode), ordering is specialty name then holder last-name-then-first, veterinarians holding nothing never enter the index, and the template is a line-for-line mirror of the existing vetList.html. Nothing behaves differently from what the diff reads as.

test_adequacy.note: The unit tests assert real outcomes, not the implementation: aSeparatelyLoadedCopyOf would fail an equality-based join, the stable-order test compares two independently-ordered assemblies, and the held-by-none and holds-nothing cases are both covered. The controller test renders the real template through MockMvc and asserts the rendered names, so the view is exercised rather than assumed.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved with empty findings, but two parked residuals in recommendations: veterinarian names in a cell are joined by a bare trailing space, so two holders render as the ambiguous run 'Helen Leary Linda Douglas'; and the security reviewer recorded that no NVD or dependency-check scan ran in this project and asked a human or CI to close it.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries and zero consultations; the one design revision was a record correction adding docs/adr/README.md to supporting_paths, not a change of design. The diff matches the requirement's stated surface exactly: one new GET page, no navigation entry, and a test that asserts no template links to it.

rationale: Contained, additive, and genuinely tested; the semantic read found no surprise. Before merging, decide on the one real residual the reviewer declined to block on: multiple veterinarians in a cell are space-joined, so names run together. Cosmetic, one template line.
